D2: The recorded cancellation fee of $6.61 must be returned in full to the rider because it was charged on a rider cancellation inside the 3-minute grace period. [F2 F5 F6] [NS-4]

D4 (VOID): The driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform never recorded him arriving at the pickup point, so NS-1 (i) and the underlying waiting-time basis are both absent. [F3 F4] [NS-1 A3]

[F1 F3 F8 F9] [NS-1]
D6: The only traffic/weather record on the corridor is a moderate speed band (20-29 km/h) on NASSIM ROAD with no incidents and fair weather, which does not explain a 1.7 km stand-off from the pickup point nor create a fee entitlement. [F10 F11 F12] [NS-1]
D7: No separate refund is due to the rider beyond the $6.61 cancellation fee, because no waiting fee or other unpublished add-on appears in the fare record and there is no surge uplift to reverse. [F5 F6] [FARE-1 NS-6]

events.body: This is a rider-filed no-show/cancellation-fee dispute. The rider cancelled, so the NS-0 branch points to NS-4: acceptance was 14:05:00 and rider cancellation at 14:07:55, i.e. 175 s (2 min 55 s) after matching [F2]. Because that is ≤ 3:00, no cancellation fee was chargeable for a rider-side cancellation under NS-4 [F2][NS-4][NS-0]. The $6.61 fee was nevertheless charged on the record [F2][F5], and no surge uplift applies (1.0×) so the entire disputed amount is the fee itself [F6][NS-0]. The fee cannot be salvaged as a driver-side no-show charge: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" [F4] and the platform never recorded arrival at the pickup [F3], and GPS shows a closest approach of 1685 m with no entry into the 200 m zone [F1], so NS-1 (i)–(iii) all fail — the driver could not have been waiting >3 minutes at the pickup [F1][F3][F4][NS-1]. NS-1 failing routes the fee back to NS-2 and the full refund outcome. The driver's own chat/statement that he was "on my way" and "about 5 min" away [F8][F9] is consistent with the GPS record rather than overriding it [F1][NS-1][NS-2]. The moderate speed band on NASSIM ROAD with no incidents and fair weather [F10][F11][F12] provides no justified-cause basis and in any event no fee entitlement under NS-1. No waiting fee or other unpublished add-on appears (only the $6.61 fee at 1.0× surge) [F5][F6][NS-6][FARE-1]. The refund is issued as a voucher per NS-7; the rider's 90-day record (1 dispute, 0 upheld) shows no abuse on the rider side [F13]. On the driver-account question, RD-6 attaches a flag only where the present case is upheld under RD-2 (refund > 0) or a RD-1 breach is recorded; this case is a rider-cancellation fee reversal under NS-4/NS-2, not an upheld route-deviation case, and the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes [F14] do not independently trigger RD-6. The trace also reports flag_account required: False. Amount = the cancellation fee charged = $6.61 [F5], equal to the trace's allowed outcome [NS-4].

events.body:
RIDER: Your cancellation fee dispute is resolved in your favour: we are refunding the full $6.61 as a Ryde voucher. You cancelled 2 minutes 55 seconds after you were matched, and no fee applies when a rider cancels within 3 minutes of matching. Your driver never marked that he had arrived and never entered the pickup area, so no no-show charge could stand either. Nothing else on your account changes; your one prior dispute with no findings against you made no difference here.

DRIVER: The rider's cancellation fee of $6.61 has been reversed and refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. The rider cancelled within 3 minutes of being matched, and because you did not mark yourself as arrived and never reached the pickup zone, no fee could be charged on your side. This means no earnings adjustment and no action on your account for this trip. No further step is needed from you.

ruling.recommended_action: Reverse the $6.61 cancellation fee and issue the rider a $6.61 Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account action against the driver on this case.
ruling.reasoning: This is a rider-filed no-show/cancellation-fee dispute. The rider cancelled, so the NS-0 branch points to NS-4: acceptance was 14:05:00 and rider cancellation at 14:07:55, i.e. 175 s (2 min 55 s) after matching [F2]. Because that is ≤ 3:00, no cancellation fee was chargeable for a rider-side cancellation under NS-4 [F2][NS-4][NS-0]. The $6.61 fee was nevertheless charged on the record [F2][F5], and no surge uplift applies (1.0×) so the entire disputed amount is the fee itself [F6][NS-0]. The fee cannot be salvaged as a driver-side no-show charge: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" [F4] and the platform never recorded arrival at the pickup [F3], and GPS shows a closest approach of 1685 m with no entry into the 200 m zone [F1], so NS-1 (i)–(iii) all fail — the driver could not have been waiting >3 minutes at the pickup [F1][F3][F4][NS-1]. NS-1 failing routes the fee back to NS-2 and the full refund outcome. The driver's own chat/statement that he was "on my way" and "about 5 min" away [F8][F9] is consistent with the GPS record rather than overriding it [F1][NS-1][NS-2]. The moderate speed band on NASSIM ROAD with no incidents and fair weather [F10][F11][F12] provides no justified-cause basis and in any event no fee entitlement under NS-1. No waiting fee or other unpublished add-on appears (only the $6.61 fee at 1.0× surge) [F5][F6][NS-6][FARE-1]. The refund is issued as a voucher per NS-7; the rider's 90-day record (1 dispute, 0 upheld) shows no abuse on the rider side [F13]. On the driver-account question, RD-6 attaches a flag only where the present case is upheld under RD-2 (refund > 0) or a RD-1 breach is recorded; this case is a rider-cancellation fee reversal under NS-4/NS-2, not an upheld route-deviation case, and the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes [F14] do not independently trigger RD-6. The trace also reports flag_account required: False. Amount = the cancellation fee charged = $6.61 [F5], equal to the trace's allowed outcome [NS-4].

rejected_claims.reason: RD-6 attaches flag_account only where the present case itself is upheld (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 route-deviation breach). Here the present case is a rider-cancellation fee reversal under NS-4/NS-2, not an upheld route deviation, and the driver's 2 prior upheld no-show disputes [F14] are a profile fact that cannot alone decide or add an account action [F14][RD-6]. The trace likewise reports flag_account required: False.

The framing that 'nothing further is warranted' beyond the voucher is rejected: the voucher form is correct under NS-7, but the rider's account record (1 dispute, 0 upheld) [F13] and the absence of any RD-2/RD-1 finding [F1][F3][F4][RD-6] mean no separate account action is created either way — the refund stands at $6.61 [F5][NS-7].

certificate: ✗ NS-4 rider cancelled more than 3 min after matching [case] 175 s after acceptance (F2)
allowed outcomes: refund_full; amount = cancellation fee $6.61

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after acceptance, i.e. within the 3-minute (≤ 3:00) window, so no cancellation fee was chargeable at all.
The $6.61 cancellation fee was nonetheless charged on the record, so that charge must be reversed in full.
No driver-side no-show case exists either: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and the driver never tapped "I'm Here".

GPS confirms the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 1685 m at the moment of cancellation and he never entered the 200 m arrival zone, so the driver was never in a position to impose a waiting or cancellation charge.

The driver's chat statement that he was "on my way" (and his own "about 5 min" estimate at 14:06) is consistent with never arriving, and in any event the statement cannot override the GPS and timeline records showing no arrival.
The charge was not a legitimate surcharge: surge multiplier was 1.0x, so the disputed $6.61 is purely the cancellation fee and the refund amount is exactly $6.61 as recorded in the fare facts.
The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days, which warrants an account review alongside the refund for repeated fee imposition.

weaknesses: The rider did cancel just 5 seconds before the 3-minute mark, so the margin is thin; the other side will argue over timestamp precision using F2 (cancelled 14:07:55 vs accepted 14:05:00) — but 175 s is still ≤ 180 s on the system record.

The driver's chat messages (F8: "About 5 min, traffic") may be used to argue the rider misled the driver or cancelled in bad faith after receiving an ETA, but chat loses to the GPS record (F1) and F8 itself concedes the driver had not arrived.
Ryde's 30-day dispute window and voucher-only refund form (NS-7) could be raised procedurally, though no fact in the index shows the request is out of time.

The compliance request against the driver is not part of the fee dispute: the rider's 90-day history shows 1 dispute, 0 upheld (F13), so no track record of the rider's own supports an abuse claim on the other side.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after acceptance, and Ryde's published rule charges the $6.61 cancellation fee only once a rider cancels later than 3 minutes after matching; since the elapsed time here is under 3:00, no fee is chargeable for a rider-side cancellation.
The recorded cancellation fee of $6.61 must be returned in full to the rider because it was charged on a rider cancellation inside the 3-minute grace period.

The fee cannot be salvaged as a no-show charge either: the driver's closest GPS approach to the pickup point over the whole trip was 1685 m and he never entered the 200 m pickup range, so NS-1 (ii) is not satisfied.
The driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform never recorded him arriving at the pickup point, so NS-1 (i) and the underlying waiting-time basis are both absent.
claims.void_reason: citation check: cites A3 — not a citable clause

claims.assertion: The driver's written statement that he 'was on his way' and his 14:06 chat estimate of 'about 5 min' cannot support a no-show charge, because NS-1 additionally requires GPS confirmation of presence at the pickup and >3 minutes of waiting there, neither of which any system record shows.

The only traffic/weather record on the corridor is a moderate speed band (20-29 km/h) on NASSIM ROAD with no incidents and fair weather, which does not explain a 1.7 km stand-off from the pickup point nor create a fee entitlement.
No separate refund is due to the rider beyond the $6.61 cancellation fee, because no waiting fee or other unpublished add-on appears in the fare record and there is no surge uplift to reverse.
The dispute was filed in the same complaint cycle as the trip, well within the 30-day window, and any refund is to be issued as a Ryde voucher of $6.61 rather than cash.

weaknesses: The driver's own 14:06 chat message promising 'about 5 min' (F8) and his statement 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled' (F9) are consistent with the rider's claim that the driver was nowhere near, and F14 shows the driver already has 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days — the other side will use these to argue a pattern of accepting trips he cannot service, and a judge could prefer escalate over a clean refund.

F2 shows the cancellation came at 2:55, only 5 seconds short of the 3-minute line; the rider side may argue the app's timestamps are approximate, and any rounding to the nearest minute would flip NS-4 against us over a few seconds.
We are conceding the centre of the case rather than defending the fee: F1 and F3-F4 make NS-1 unarguable, so we cannot claim the $4.50 driver share or resist the refund on any factual ground.

points.response: Agreed and relied on: F2 puts the cancellation at 2 min 55 s after acceptance, inside the 3:00 window, so under NS-4 no rider-side cancellation fee is chargeable.
Agreed: the $6.61 recorded in the fare facts must be returned in full, and the absence of any surge uplift (F6) means the whole disputed amount is the fee itself.
Agreed: F1 (closest approach 1685 m, never within 200 m) plus F3 satisfies neither NS-1 (ii) nor NS-1 (iii), so the fee cannot be re-characterised as a no-show charge.
Agreed, and we add that the driver's "about 5 min" estimate (F8) was still outstanding at cancellation, so even his own account in F9 cannot establish arrival at the pickup.

Agreed: the only corridor record is a moderate speed band of 20-29 km/h on NASSIM ROAD with no incidents and fair weather (F10, F11, F12), which explains neither a 1.7 km stand-off nor any fee entitlement; the driver raised no justified-cause defence.
Noted and agreed: we claim only the $6.61 cancellation fee and seek no additional waiting-fee or unpublished-charge refund, consistent with FARE-1 and NS-6 on this fare record (F5, F6).

We accept the voucher form of the refund under NS-7 but not the framing that nothing further is warranted: F14 shows 2 upheld no-show disputes against this driver in 90 days, which supports an account-review flag alongside the refund under NS-2.
Conceded on the merits: F2 records acceptance at 14:05:00 and rider cancellation at 14:07:55 = 175 s, inside the ≤ 3:00 window, so under NS-4 no cancellation fee was chargeable.
Conceded: the fare record shows the $6.61 cancellation fee was in fact charged (F5) and NS-0 allows the NS-4 branch to reach it, so the charge is reversed in full.
Accepted, and it is the driver's own case: driver_arrived_at is null and no "I'm Here" tap exists (F3, F4), so NS-1 (i) and (ii) both fail and NS-2 governs.
Accepted: the closest GPS approach of 1685 m with no entry into the 200 m zone (F1) confirms the driver never reached the pickup, which is exactly why NS-1 fails and no fee can stand.

Conceded in part: chat does not decide the case, but F8's "About 5 min" and F9's "on my way" (F8, F9) are the driver's own contemporaneous statement that he had not arrived, and they are consistent with the GPS record (F1, F3) rather than in conflict with it.
Conceded: surge was 1.0x (F6), so the disputed amount is purely the $6.61 cancellation fee (F5) and the refund is exactly $6.61 with nothing else to strip out.

Contested: F14 shows 2 upheld no-show disputes out of 666 completed trips in 90 days, and RD-6 attaches flag_account only where the present case itself is upheld (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) — this case is not upheld, so no account action is warranted here.
The rider side's C2 and C6 reach the same figure the driver requested in D2 ($6.61 via NS-4), so the only live dispute is C7's flag_account request, which fails for the reason above.
